name: Shardflux

modes.label: Workspace
modes.note: docs.shardflux.dev/limits (2026-09-29): CPU hours = CPU time the workspace's processes actually used, overage $0.12 per CPU-hour; RAM GiB-hours = memory allocation while the workspace runs, overage $0.04 per GiB-hour. Suspended workspaces use neither. Runs in AWS us-west-2 only.

modes.label: File-first workspace (fresh VM per command)
modes.note: RAM counted only while an execution runs, at the execution VM's memory; file-first workspaces never count toward running workspaces at once; one execution at a time per workspace; no processes survive between commands. Same $0.12/CPU-hour and $0.04/GiB-hour overage rates (docs.shardflux.dev/limits, 2026-09-29).

evidence.quote: effective = workspace override > project policy > platform default (allow_all).
Outbound transfer 10 GB 100 GB 1 TB 5 TB
At 100 %, outbound internet traffic of every workspace in the organization is blocked until you upgrade, add more, or the next period starts.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Free: CPU/RAM hours 'as available' on spare capacity, measured but not capped; no overage; 3 running at once; 1 vCPU / 2 GiB / 2 GiB disk; 10 GiB retained; 10 GB egress; 1 shared volume of 1 GiB. Allowances reset each calendar month (UTC).

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: Includes 100 CPU-hours + 800 RAM GiB-hours, valued here at the overage rates ($12 + $32 = $44). 10 workspaces at once, 100 GiB retained storage, 100 GB outgoing transfer (blocked beyond it).

plans.name: Startup
plans.note: Includes 400 CPU-hours + 3,200 RAM GiB-hours, valued at the overage rates ($48 + $128 = $176). 50 workspaces at once, 1,000 GiB retained storage, 1 TB outgoing transfer.

plans.name: Scale
plans.note: Includes 1,000 CPU-hours + 8,000 RAM GiB-hours, valued at the overage rates ($120 + $320 = $440). 200 workspaces at once, 3,000 GiB retained storage, 5 TB outgoing transfer.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom limits and a shared concurrency ceiling for the organisation.

features.ip_note: Egress/IP options not documented; outgoing transfer is capped per plan and blocked at 100%.

caveats: Plans include CPU-hours and RAM GiB-hours, not dollars. They are valued at the published overage rates ($0.12/CPU-hour, $0.04/GiB-hour) so the engine can net them against usage; in reality the two allowances do not offset each other, so a workload that uses up only one of them can cost somewhat more than shown.
Overage is off until you turn it on, with a spend cap you set (shardflux.dev pricing, 2026-09-29).

Retained storage (suspended workspaces, shared volumes) is never charged; outgoing transfer has no overage price and is blocked when the plan allowance runs out, so egress beyond the allowance is priced as unknown.

Every workspace is its own microVM with its own kernel; the hypervisor is not named. Suspend checkpoints memory and processes; resume p50 0.3 s, new workspace p50 0.2 s (vendor claims on the landing page).
Templates (e.g. python-node-browser) are the base images; whether you can bring a Dockerfile/OCI image is not documented. Docker inside, nested virtualisation, root and SSH are not documented.
Workspaces run in AWS us-west-2 only; no data residency outside the United States. Start waits up to 15 minutes for capacity before failing with capacity_unavailable.
Features set to null were not verified. No workspace was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims.

Opt-in overage is capped at most at the plan price ($9/$79/$299), so a month's bill is at most 2x the plan fee; beyond that, starts are refused and running workspaces are suspended (402 spend_cap_reached). Large workloads need Enterprise.

Idle-but-running workspaces bill full RAM: hosts 'park' idle workspaces but they stay running and use their full allocation. The adaptive idle timeout is 5 min until learned (10 s to 4 h), or it can be set to fixed:60-604800 s or never.
Rate limits: 3,600 tool tokens per hour per API key (an open that returns a token counts; 429 rate_limited beyond), 3 concurrent template builds per org.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A persistent workspace suspends itself when it has been idle for its idle timeout. Nothing is killed: the suspend keeps memory and processes like any other.
snapshot_auto.note: Triggers: idle timeout (adaptive 10 s-4 h, default 5 min until learned; or fixed:60-604800 s / never), suspend-when-idle requests, compute allowance or spend cap. Memory + processes + disk checkpointed (Firecracker snapshot) and restored on resume; after a rare platform runtime change a resume cold-boots from disk (memory_restored:false). Session-lifetime workspaces are deleted instead.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: records a checkpoint of a running or suspended workspace without stopping it. While a running workspace is captured, reads work and writes wait. The API has no call to list or restore snapshots yet; to branch from a state, [fork](#fork-a-workspace).
snapshot_on_demand.note: snapshot() exists but cannot yet be listed/restored. The usable on-demand path is fork: 'a copy of its disk and memory, restored into an independent VM' from a running or suspended workspace (memory included, boots new workspaces). Also save-as-template (disk only, new template layer) and reset keeps a 7-day recovery point.

harness_api.quote: Your harness runs the model loop and your own tools.
harness_api.note: Model is inverted: your agent/harness runs outside and gets workspace tools (TS/Python tool definitions, MCP server for Claude Code/Cursor/Codex/Claude Desktop). No API to start/stream/resume Claude Code or another harness inside the workspace was found.

egress_allowlist.quote: mode allow_all | allowlist | deny_all; rules/cidrs only with allowlist. Hosts: exact FQDN or `*.` single-label wildcard (IDNA-normalized, lower-case); IP literals and localhost-like names are rejected. Ports 1-65535 (default [443]); protocols tcp only. cidrs: public ranges only.
egress_allowlist.note: Per project (default) and per-workspace override, versioned; template versions can set an egress ceiling the workspace cannot widen. Enforced by the host ('effective_policy: what the host enforces'), enforcement state reported. Also CLI: shard egress set. Build network for templates: auto/none/allowlist.

egress_http_rules.note: Rules are host + ports (TCP) plus CIDRs only; no method/path/header rules documented.

guest_firewall.note: Each workspace is a Firecracker microVM 'with its own kernel'; ubuntu-24.04 base includes sudo and template build steps run as root. iptables/nftables not mentioned in docs.

secret_proxy.quote:
Every command and terminal in the workspace
gets it as an environment variable, and no API ever returns the value.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are write-only in the API but injected as env vars into every exec/PTY (secret_refs per process), so the value is inside the VM. Per-secret allowedWorkspaceIds/allowedTools, rotation, org secrets with access logs. No credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Attach a shared volume to a workspace at mount_path (ro or rw).
volume_attach.note: Shared volumes are EFS access points ('Create a shared volume (EFS access point created by the cell)'); up to 8 per workspace; hot-attach into a running guest; plan limits 1x1 GiB (Free) to 100x1,000 GiB (Scale); storage not charged. Outside memory checkpoints.

volume_shared.quote: Persistent volumes shared between workspaces of a project.
volume_shared.note: Read-write or read-only per attachment; EFS-backed; org_shared volumes attachable from every project; forks attach (not copy) the same volume: 'Shared volumes are attached, not copied: both see the same data.'

image_oci.quote: recipe | TemplateRecipeV1 or TemplateRecipeV2 | yes | Recipe v1 (TemplateRecipeV1: a Dockerfile, no `schema` field) or recipe v2
image_oci.note: Templates can be built from a Dockerfile (recipe v1); this builds a versioned template image rather than opening a workspace directly from an arbitrary pre-built OCI image, but it is the documented way to bring your own container definition.

nested_virt.quote: each a Firecracker microVM with its own kernel
nested_virt.note: derived: Firecracker microVMs do not expose /dev/kvm or nested virtualization to the guest by default, and no docs mention it.

desktop.quote: `browser` | Browser | Screenshots and rendered page content from the workspace's headless browser
desktop.note: not offered: the only browser surface is a headless Chromium (screenshot/content), not a graphical desktop (VNC/RDP/stream).

computer_use.quote: POST /browser/screenshot, POST /browser/content | browser | Navigates the workspace's headless Chromium; returns a PNG, or the rendered page as HTML or text.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no click/type/mouse API against the screenshot, only navigate+screenshot/content of a headless browser.

anti_bot.quote: Shardflux gives AI agents persistent, isolated cloud computers called workspaces.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Shardflux is a general dev-sandbox/microVM platform with a plain headless Chromium; no stealth/fingerprinting features are documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Shardflux gives AI agents persistent, isolated cloud computers called workspaces.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature is documented anywhere in the docs or reference.

egress_ip_type.quote: It does not fit calls from a browser or mobile app, workspaces larger than 16 vCPU and 32 GiB RAM, or data that must stay outside AWS us-west-2.
egress_ip_type.note: Workspaces run as AWS microVMs in us-west-2 only; no residential/mobile egress product is offered or documented, so outbound IPs are ordinary datacenter (AWS) addresses.

ssh.quote: Tool | Console label | Allows | exec Run commands | files Read and write files | pty Terminal sessions | Interactive terminals | process Background processes | git Git | browser Browser
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. All command/terminal access is through the API's exec/pty tools via a tool token at the workspace's cell_endpoint; no SSH server or key-based SSH access is documented.

agent_harnesses.quote: Your harness runs the model loop and your own tools.
agent_harnesses.note: The model is inverted: coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Claude Desktop) run outside and call Shardflux workspace tools over MCP/SDK; no harness is preinstalled or offered as a template inside a workspace. Only template is python-node-browser (a runtime stack) and ubuntu-24.04 (a bare base).

own_agent_api.quote: Shardflux gives AI agents persistent, isolated cloud computers called workspaces.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Shardflux provides sandboxes/tools for your own agent; it has no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent of its own.

public_ipv4.quote: Workspace tools (exec, PTY, processes, files, git, browser) are served by the workspace's cell at its cell_endpoint
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. All interaction happens through Shardflux's own API/cell_endpoint proxy; no per-workspace public IPv4 address is documented.

inbound_https.quote: Outbound transfer | Bytes your workspaces send to the internet, in decimal GB. Inbound traffic is free and does not count
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Docs discuss outbound transfer and egress allowlists at length but never describe an HTTPS URL/ingress mechanism to reach a port a workspace listens on from the public internet.

ingress_rules.quote: Outbound network policy of a project or a workspace.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The only documented network policy object (allow_all/allowlist/deny_all, hosts, ports, CIDRs) is explicitly an outbound/egress policy; no inbound/ingress control surface is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Fork | A fork creates a new workspace ... restored into an independent VM with its own network identity.
static_egress_ip.note: Not documented as a feature; a fork explicitly gets a new network identity, implying outbound IPs are not fixed/stable per workspace and no static/dedicated egress IP product is offered.

gpu.quote: It does not fit calls from a browser or mobile app, workspaces larger than 16 vCPU and 32 GiB RAM, or data that must stay outside AWS us-west-2.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only vCPU/RAM sizing (up to 16 vCPU / 32 GiB) is documented; no GPU option appears anywhere in pricing, limits or templates.

self_host.quote: Shardflux (https://shardflux.dev) is a hosted service by Helios One Oy.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Shardflux is explicitly a hosted SaaS product with no self-hosting/on-prem deployment documented.

byoc.quote: Shardflux (https://shardflux.dev) is a hosted service by Helios One Oy.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Workspaces run only in Shardflux's own AWS us-west-2 account; no bring-your-own-cloud deployment is documented.

open_source.note: The client SDK package is Apache-2.0, but that is only a thin client library; the core workspace platform/service itself is closed-source with no public repo found.

max_session_h.quote: persistent (the default) | Ends | Only when you delete it
max_session_h.note: A persistent workspace has no documented maximum continuous runtime; it only suspends automatically when idle (adaptive/fixed idle timeout) or when a compute allowance/spend cap is hit, not on a fixed wall-clock session length.

windows.quote: Shardflux gives AI agents cloud computers. Each workspace is a Linux microVM with its own kernel, disk and memory.
windows.note: Product is Linux-microVM-only; no Windows machine option is documented anywhere in the docs/pricing. Outside the product's scope.

macos.quote: Shardflux gives AI agents cloud computers. Each workspace is a Linux microVM with its own kernel, disk and memory.
macos.note: Same Linux-microVM-only product; no macOS offering documented. Outside the product's scope.

eu_data_residency.quote: Workspaces and the API run in AWS us-west-2 (Oregon, United States).
eu_data_residency.note: Single-region deployment (US only); no EU region or data-residency option is offered anywhere in the docs.

live_resize.quote: caps ... Optional user caps; the ceiling is min(template, cap, plan).
live_resize.note: caps (vCPU/RAM/disk) are only set on open/fork/create and are 'fixed while the workspace runs' (limits page); there is no PATCH/update-caps endpoint on a running workspace — changing size requires a new open/fork, not a live resize.

arm64.quote: Workspaces and the API run in AWS us-west-2 (Oregon, United States).
arm64.note: No ARM/aarch64/Graviton machine option, base image, or template architecture is mentioned anywhere in the docs, pricing, template base list (ubuntu-24.04, python-node-browser), or the template-build error code architecture_not_supported (which refers to build/base compatibility, not a documented ARM offering). Firecracker microVMs on a single AWS x86 region with no ARM base published indicates ARM is not offered.

usage_api.quote: GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/usage: Usage of one workspace (time series and totals). Meter options: cpu_seconds, memory_gib_seconds, storage_gib_seconds, egress_bytes, ingress_bytes, volume_storage_gib_seconds.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: no; Shardflux provides a workspace-level usage API returning billable quantities (CPU seconds, memory GiB-seconds, storage) with hourly or daily granularity. Cost is available through a separate estimate API (GET /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/usage/estimate), so the usage endpoint returns quantities only.

locations_quote: Workspaces and the API run in AWS us-west-2 (Oregon, United States).
